jobs.description:
Arquitecto de Datos Senior
Modalidad: 100% remoto (cualquier país), trabajando en horario Argentina (ART) | Seniority: Senior (4+ años)

Contexto del rol
Buscamos un Arquitecto de Datos Senior para liderar la evolución de una plataforma de datos actualmente
basada en SQL Server + SSIS + SSAS hacia una arquitectura moderna en cloud. El perfil deberá definir la
arquitectura target, planificar la migración por fases, establecer estándares técnicos y guiar al Data Engineer,
sosteniendo en paralelo las necesidades analíticas actuales del cliente: reporting, modelos de churn y

segmentación.

El stack target todavía no está cerrado. El cliente cuenta con infraestructura AWS, pero se busca un perfil con
criterio agnóstico, capaz de evaluar alternativas y recomendar la mejor arquitectura para el caso de negocio.

  • Industria: aseguradora. Proyecto de modernización de plataforma de datos y migración progresiva desde stack
    legacy on-prem hacia cloud/lakehouse/DWH moderno.

Responsabilidades principales

  • Diseñar la arquitectura target del data platform: ingesta, almacenamiento, transformación, serving y
    gobierno.
  • Definir el camino de migración desde SQL Server / SSIS / SSAS hacia tecnología cloud, combinando
    lakehouse y DWH cuando corresponda.
  • Establecer estándares de modelado, calidad, lineage y gobierno de datos.
  • Diseñar patrones reutilizables de pipelines y orquestación.
  • Definir estrategia de reemplazo o evolución del semantic layer de SSAS, incluyendo cubos tabulares / MDX, en el nuevo stack.
  • Trabajar con stakeholders del cliente, traduciendo necesidades de negocio a soluciones técnicas.
  • Mentorear al Data Engineer y revisar implementaciones.
  • Habilitar casos de uso analíticos avanzados como modelos de churn, segmentación y reporting.
  • Evaluar alternativas tecnológicas con criterio agnóstico, considerando que el stack target aún no está cerrado.
  • Balancear evolución cloud con convivencia temporal del stack legacy.

Requisitos (must-have)

  • 4+ años de experiencia en data, con experiencia hands-on y no únicamente arquitectura conceptual.
  • Experiencia sólida con SQL Server y SSIS para convivir con el stack legacy del cliente.
  • Experiencia comprobable en migraciones de datos desde on-prem hacia cloud.
  • Python productivo.
  • Airflow productivo.
  • Modelado dimensional sólido, especialmente Kimball.
  • Entendimiento de OBT (One Big Table) y criterios de uso.
  • Experiencia con Cloud Data Warehouse moderno: Redshift, Snowflake, BigQuery o Synapse.
  • Conocimiento/experiencia en arquitectura lakehouse: Databricks, Delta Lake o Iceberg.
  • Diseño de pipelines escalables y observables.
  • Fundamentos de gobierno de datos: calidad, lineage y catálogo.
  • Seguridad en cloud: IAM, encryption y RBAC.
  • Capacidad de interactuar con stakeholders no técnicos y traducir necesidades de negocio a soluciones de datos.
  • Capacidad de tomar decisiones con incertidumbre y justificar trade-offs.
  • Disponibilidad para trabajar 100% remoto en horario Argentina.

Diferenciales / Deseables

  • ﻿AWS hands-on: S3, Glue, Redshift, Athena, EMR, Lake Formation (diferencial fuerte por infraestructura
    existente del cliente).
  • Haber diseñado pipelines para modelos de churn: feature engineering, training, scoring y monitoring.dbt.
  • DataOps / CI-CD para datos: Git, Terraform, testing de pipelines.
  • Streaming / event-driven: Kafka o Kinesis.
  • Certificaciones AWS, Azure o GCP en data.
  • Experiencia específica reemplazando o modernizando SSAS / semantic layer.
  • Experiencia en gobierno de datos con catálogos, lineage y estándares de calidad.
  • Inglés técnico de lectura, no mandatorio.

Soft skills

  • ﻿Comunicación clara con stakeholders no técnicos.
  • Liderazgo técnico y capacidad de mentoría.
  • Orientación a negocio e impacto.
  • Autonomía para definir arquitectura con información incompleta.
  • Criterio para priorizar fases de migración y reducir riesgo operativo.
  • Capacidad de documentar decisiones y estándares.
  • Disciplina para trabajar remoto en coordinación con horario Argentina.

Compensación y Beneficios

  • Pago en dólares estadounidenses (USD).
  • Modalidad full-time. Duración inicial de 5 meses, con posibilidad de
    continuar de forma indeterminada.
  • Ingreso inmediato.

jobs.description:
About us

OpenZeppelin is the security standard onchain finance is built on. Founded in 2015, our mission is to accelerate the world's transition to an open financial system, built on open standards and secured by rigorous research.

Our open-source Contract Libraries have facilitated over $35 trillion in onchain value and are used by 10 of the top 10 tokenized money market funds and 9 of the top 10 stablecoins by market cap.

We combine AI-native security tooling with deep research and a decade of audit expertise to support leading institutions and crypto-native teams shaping the next generation of digital assets like DTCC, Fidelity, Coinbase, Uniswap, Aave, the Ethereum Foundation, and many more across the full secure development lifecycle.

Please note: Always refer to OpenZeppelin's official job page for the most accurate information about our open roles, as we have seen multiple third party job sites posting inaccurate information.

The Secure Development team ❤️

OpenZeppelin is the security partner of choice for the most important protocols in Web3. Our Secure Development team sits at the intersection of building and breaking: we design, implement, and harden production-grade libraries and smart contracts for leading projects across EVM, Starknet, Stellar/Soroban, Arbitrum Stylus, Aptos, and beyond, often as an embedded extension of the client's engineering team.

We work the way the rest of the industry will five years from now. Every developer on the team is a fully AI-native engineer, supported by outstanding internal AI tooling built for every phase of secure development. Developers own their workstreams end-to-end — agents amplify their effectiveness, and peers, security researchers, and external auditors provide rigorous review on every piece of work that ships.

The Canton Network engagement

This role joins an active 24-month, multi-million-dollar commitment to build the open-source DeFi foundations of the world's most institutional blockchain. You'll deliver production-ready Reference Implementations (privacy-preserving DEX, lending, cross-chain stablecoin settlement, confidential auction launchpad, and more), the OpenZeppelin Contracts Library for Daml that Canton developers will import, and Canton standards implementation.

Within this, you will:

  • Own features of the OpenZeppelin Contracts Library for Daml end to end, from design through audit: examples include a Timelock, access control, vaults, or token standard support.
  • Design and implement components of the year-1 Reference Implementations: privacy-preserving DEX, lending protocol, cross-chain stablecoin settlement, and confidential auction launchpad.
  • Implement and shepherd the OZ Daml versions of CIP-56, CIP-86, CIP-103, future CIPs. Coordinate with Digital Asset on spec evolution and with ChainSafe on middleware alignment.
  • Present and defend your designs in technical discussions with Digital Asset, the Canton Foundation, and other partners.
  • Work with OpenZeppelin's security researchers on threat models, audit preparation, and fixes for the components you own.
  • Use AI systems as core daily tools for research, design, implementation, testing, and security work. Build agents, skills, and workflows, and share what works with the team.
  • Contribute developer-experience and security feedback upstream into the Canton protocol, Splice, the Daml SDK, and the Splice Wallet Kernel.
  • Research privacy-preserving DeFi, multi-party authorization patterns, and Canton-specific primitives, and share what you learn with the team.

You have

  • Production Daml fluency. You understand templates, choices, controllers/observers/signatories, multi-party authorization, sub-transaction views, and propose/accept patterns as first-class primitives. Running an SV, contributing to Splice internals, governance, or Canton Coin tokenomics.
  • Canton architecture depth. You understand the network, not only the code: the Global Synchronizer and private synchronizers, what each party and synchronizer sees in a transaction, smart contract upgrades, and the token standards (CIP-56, CIP-112).
  • 3+ years of smart contract development in production. This includes hands-on work on Canton or another UTXO-based or privacy-preserving architecture (Cardano, Midnight, Zcash, Aleo, Mina, or similar). You can reason about Canton's privacy boundaries the way an EVM developer reasons about storage slots.
  • Production DeFi experience. You have shipped DeFi primitives such as AMMs, vaults (ERC-4626 or equivalent), lending protocols, or cross-chain settlement, and you understand the security pitfalls of each. You know the standard EVM patterns (access control, token standards, lending pools, DEXs), because many Canton standards reuse them.
  • A security-first mindset. This is non-negotiable. You build secure code by default, you think adversarially about every line you write, and you find vulnerabilities when you review Daml code. We look for a developer with a security mindset, not a security researcher. Published audits, threat models, or disclosures are a plus.
  • An AI-native workflow. Claude Code, Cursor, or equivalent is your daily driver. You know agents, harnesses, and skills, not only autocomplete. You hold AI output to the same standard as a colleague's pull request, and you stay accountable for everything you ship.
  • Fluency in client-facing communication (English)
  • Autonomy and proactivity.

Nice to have

  • Cryptography or financial-engineering background. Privacy-preserving DeFi rewards both.
  • Institutional finance and compliance design experience. Credential gates, multi-party attestation, custody flows, capital-markets microstructure, RWA tokenization, settlement.
  • Experience running an SV, contributing to Splice internals, governance, or Canton Coin tokenomics.
  • Cross-chain interoperability exposure. Production work with at least one major cross-chain messaging protocol (Chainlink CCIP, LayerZero, Wormhole, Axelar, or similar).
  • Library / SDK API design taste. You've built reusable, import-first developer libraries, not just applications. You have opinions on extensibility patterns (hooks, modular components, override points) and on what makes an audited primitive pleasant to consume.
  • Experience applying AI to security work. You've already used AI as a serious instrument in security workflows: audit assistance, vulnerability research, fuzzing, invariant or spec analysis, static-analysis augmentation, or similar.
  • Hands-on experience with non-EVM ecosystems. Starknet, Stellar/Soroban, Arbitrum Stylus, Aptos, Move-based chains.
  • Open-source contributions to widely-used libraries in the smart-contract or AI-tooling space.

Logistics

Our interview process is designed to be fast (we target ~30 days from first call to offer) while still giving both sides a clear "yes." The full process consists of:

  • Recruiter interview (30-45 minutes)
  • Manager interview (60 minutes)
  • Team interview (45 minutes)
  • Leadership Interview (30 minutes)
  • Paid technical work trial

Please let us know if you require any accommodations for the interview process, and we’ll do our best to provide assistance.

Benefits

  • Meet your teammates at company gatherings around the world 😎
  • Enjoy the flexibility of fully remote work 🌎
  • Take the time you need with flexible time off 🏝
  • Grow your family with 8 weeks of paid leave for primary caregivers, 4 weeks for secondary caregivers, and a one-time $3,600 baby bonus 💙
  • Build your ideal home office with up to $500 in equipment support 🪑
  • Stay covered with medical insurance 🏥
  • Keep growing with learning and development opportunities 🧠
  • Get a monthly stipend for your preferred co-working space 💻

At OpenZeppelin, we are an equal opportunity employer and we value different perspectives. We are committed to building a diverse workforce. This includes but is not limited to gender, race, sexual orientation, religion, national origin and other characteristics that make each one of us unique. In this uniqueness, we find the most value. Come join us!

Use of AI as part of the recruiting process

As part of OpenZeppelin’s recruitment process, we may use automated tools, including artificial intelligence, to assist in reviewing applications and assessing candidate qualifications. These tools are used to support our People team by identifying relevant skills and experience, and are not used to make decisions solely by automated means. All hiring decisions involve human review. Any personal data provided as part of your application will be processed in accordance with OpenZeppelin’s Data Privacy Notice.

If you have questions about this recruitment process or would like to request human review of your application, please contact us at .

Join the Content Domain team of a major retail organisation as a Senior Content Modeller, shaping the next phase of an enterprise-scale headless content platform. As adoption has spread across teams, familiar challenges have emerged: content models that are hard to discover and understand, inconsistent decisions between reuse and new model creation, fragmented documentation, and modelling decisions reviewed too late in delivery cycles. jobs.title: Forward-Deployed CRM Architect
jobs.excerpt: RevOps is changing fast, and so is the way GTM processes get built and maintained inside the CRM.
jobs.description:
RevOps is changing fast, and so is the way GTM processes get built and maintained inside the CRM. This role puts you on the front edge of it: forward-deployed in our clients' RevOps teams, building and running their GTM systems in a genuinely AI-first environment.

GTMBase is an AI-first GTM engineering and RevOps agency. We help post-PMF B2B companies (€8M to €50M ARR, 5+ reps) whose go-to-market is over-performing their systems. Reps do manually what should be automated, sales and marketing data doesn't connect, and leadership can't trust the reporting.

We combine strategic GTM thinking with hands-on technical build, and we fix the foundation before running campaigns.

We deliver across Four Pillars:

  1. Data Foundation: list building and enrichment so reps win with better data (Clay, Apollo, custom scrapers, AI research)
  2. RevOps & CRM: building the right GTM process inside the client's CRM, including architecture, lifecycle, pipelines, routing, and reporting (HubSpot, Salesforce)
  3. Agentic Workflows: building agentic GTM workflows with Anthropic Managed Agents and Hermes, getting the org ready for Agentic GTM
  4. GTM Strategy & Plays: recommending and executing the highest-impact campaigns

We've done this for clients including Groupon, Blinkist, Booksy, and Sendify. We work in small pods, with a Strategist, a CRM Architect, and a GTM Engineer.

How We Operate

We run the company on Claude Code. It's our operating system: client context, playbooks, automations, and delivery all live in it, and AI is the default way we work rather than a bolt-on. You'll work this way too, and get very good at it.

Why This Role Matters

You're the person who turns our GTM strategy into a CRM that actually works. Most clients run their entire revenue motion on HubSpot or Salesforce, and the quality of that system runs through this role: how clean the data is, how well leads route, whether leadership can trust the reporting.

Here, "Architect" means architecting inside the CRM: the object model, pipelines, workflows, and automations. The GTM and revenue strategy is set with you in your pod, not by you alone, and you build it with real craft.

You're forward-deployed: you embed with clients' RevOps and sales teams and build inside their live CRM.

The Role

You'll build and maintain GTM process and automation inside our clients' CRMs, mostly HubSpot. Working from the direction set in your pod, you turn requirements into a clean, well-built system the sales team can rely on.

One week you're building a client's lead lifecycle and routing. The next you're debugging a broken automation, untangling duplicate deals, or shipping a dashboard a CRO asked for. You move across several client instances at once without dropping threads.

You're a builder with an admin's discipline. You know the object model, not just the UI. You sweat the details others miss, you test before you ship, and you document what you build so the rest of the pod can run it. When something breaks, you find the root cause and fix it properly.

How This Differs From a GTM Engineer

Your pod is you (CRM Architect), a Strategist who sets direction and hands you requirements, and a GTM Engineer. You and the GTM Engineer are both builders, but you own different layers:

  • You (CRM Architect, Pillar 2): the GTM process inside the CRM. HubSpot/Salesforce architecture, lifecycle, routing, deal logic, automation, reporting, data integrity. You live in HubSpot, Salesforce, Operations Hub, and n8n.
  • GTM Engineer (Pillar 1): the data layer. Enrichment, scraping, signal detection, list building, custom research agents. They live in Clay, Apify, custom scrapers, and data APIs.

Think of it as the data into the CRM (GTM Engineer) versus the system it lands in and the process the sales team runs on (you). You don't need to be a Clay or Apify expert. You just need a solid working understanding of what a GTM Engineer does, enough to spec what you need, integrate their output cleanly, and know what's possible.

What You'll Do

  • Architect and build in client HubSpot instances: information architecture (objects, associations, lifecycle stages, pipeline structure), workflows, deal logic, lead scoring, routing, properties, and permissions
  • Build and debug automations across the GTM stack: HubSpot workflows, n8n, APIs, and webhooks. When an automation breaks, you find the root cause rather than just toggling features
  • Guard data integrity: deduplication, field validation, association hygiene, and import discipline so reporting and forecasting can be trusted
  • Build the reporting leadership relies on: pipeline coverage and velocity, stage-by-stage conversion, and full-funnel dashboards. You know where HubSpot's platform and paywall limits force a different approach
  • Design integrations and data flows between HubSpot and the rest of the stack (Clay, Aircall, telephony, billing, enrichment pipelines)
  • Turn requirements into working builds: take a brief like a 15-minute lead-response SLA and ship the routing system that delivers it
  • Keep multiple client instances healthy at once, with fast turnaround and nothing falling through the cracks
  • Work client-facing: you can talk through a data question with a technical lead and walk a frustrated AE through a new flow in the same afternoon
  • Codify what works into our library of reusable plays and patterns, so every client build sharpens the whole team

What We're Looking For

Must-have

  • Deep HubSpot expertise: hands-on across Sales, Marketing, Service, and Operations Hubs. You know HubSpot well enough to know what is and isn't possible at the platform level, and to choose native functionality over a workaround when it's the right call.
  • Strong CRM and RevOps fundamentals: lead lifecycle and qualification, routing and assignment, pipeline and deal-stage setup, the data model, and the governance that keeps it clean.
  • An admin's discipline: precise, reliable, and detail-obsessed. You test before you ship, you keep data clean, and you don't let things fall through the cracks.
  • A builder's instinct: you build workflows and integrations, debug them when they break, and aren't intimidated by APIs, webhooks, or a tool you haven't used yet.
  • AI-first, and we mean it literally: AI is your default operating mode, not a novelty. Your first move on a problem is to reach for an agent, a prompt, or a workflow before a manual process. If you're not already using AI tools daily, this isn't the right fit. (If your CRM fundamentals are deep but your GTM-tooling experience like Clay or Claude Code is light, that part is learnable and we'll back you on it. The fundamentals and the AI-first instinct are not.)
  • Forward-deployed temperament: comfortable building across multiple clients in parallel, client-facing, proactive, and able to move fast without waiting for perfect requirements.
  • Full-time availability with reliable overlap to CET hours.

Nice-to-have

  • Salesforce: admin or build experience, especially HubSpot to Salesforce sync and migrations (relevant to Groupon and enterprise work)
  • A working understanding of the GTM Engineer's toolkit: Clay, Apify, enrichment providers (ZoomInfo, Apollo, Clearbit), scraping. Enough to collaborate, spec, and integrate. Your pod's GTM Engineer owns the deep builds.
  • n8n orchestration and custom API integrations
  • Scripting (Python, SQL, or JavaScript) for data manipulation and custom connectors
  • German: a good chunk of our client base is DACH
  • HubSpot certifications: a plus, never a gate. Demonstrated depth matters more.

What You'll Get

  • Real client build work from day one, with no busy work and no hand-holding
  • A front-row seat in a genuinely AI-first environment: Claude Code as the operating system, Clay, and the full modern GTM stack
  • Direct collaboration with one of the most experienced RevOps leaders in Europe
  • Exposure to a wide range of B2B companies, stacks, and GTM problems
  • A seat at the table in a growing practice, not a cog in a machine

jobs.description:
This is a remote position.

Our client is looking for a Clinical Operations Medical Assistant to support patients, prescribing providers, and the daily administrative operations of a growing psychiatric practice. They operate within the virtual mental health industry and have expanded their services across multiple U.S. markets while building a larger team of affirming behavioral health providers.

This role combines patient communication, healthcare administration, prior authorizations, insurance coordination, medication-related support, and provider assistance. The ideal candidate is organized, proactive, dependable, and comfortable managing several priorities independently in a remote environment.

The right professional will bring experience supporting U.S. healthcare workflows and a demonstrated commitment to respectful, inclusive, and LGBTQIA+-affirming patient care.

Responsibilities
  • Manage patient communications through approved phone, messaging, and healthcare platforms.
  • Coordinate patient appointments, scheduling changes, and follow-up activities.
  • Assist patients with administrative questions related to forms, referrals, prescriptions, insurance, and appointments.
  • Follow up on incomplete forms, missing documentation, referrals, and outstanding patient requests.
  • Review patient charts to identify medication authorization requirements.
  • Prepare, submit, monitor, and follow up on prior authorization requests.
  • Coordinate with insurance companies regarding medication coverage, approvals, denials, and appeals.
  • Communicate with pharmacies regarding prescriptions, refill requests, authorization requirements, and medication availability.
  • Support prescribing providers with medication-related administrative workflows.
  • Process verbal refill orders when permitted and properly authorized.
  • Complete insurance eligibility and benefits verification.
  • Assist with referral management and claims-related communication.
  • Maintain accurate, confidential, and updated information within electronic health record systems.
  • Organize tasks and priorities to ensure requests are completed within expected timelines.
  • Maintain clear documentation of patient, pharmacy, provider, and insurance interactions.
  • Follow HIPAA requirements and internal healthcare compliance procedures.
  • Identify workflow gaps and contribute to the development or improvement of standard operating procedures.
  • Learn and adopt new healthcare software platforms as the practice continues to grow.

Requirements

  • At least 1 year of experience in healthcare administration, clinical operations, behavioral health, or a medical office environment.
  • Ideally 2 or more years of relevant healthcare administrative experience.
  • Hands-on experience managing prior authorizations with limited supervision.
  • Experience handling confidential patient information and following HIPAA requirements.
  • Familiarity with U.S. healthcare insurance, pharmacy, and medication approval workflows.
  • Experience using electronic health record or electronic medical record systems.
  • Excellent written and verbal English communication skills.
  • Strong patient service and professional communication abilities.
  • Excellent organization, prioritization, and time-management skills.
  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision.
  • Ability to manage several patient and provider requests simultaneously.
  • Demonstrated experience supporting LGBTQIA+ patients or communities.
  • Commitment to inclusive, affirming, and patient-centered care.
  • Proficiency with Google Workspace, Microsoft Office, or similar productivity tools.
  • Ability to learn new technology and healthcare platforms quickly.
  • Availability to work during U.S. Eastern Time business hours.
  • Reliable high-speed internet and a professional remote workspace.
  • A dependable backup plan for power or internet disruptions.
  • Ability to use the client’s approved VPN when accessing U.S.-based systems.
  • Ability to maintain reliable overlap with provider, patient, pharmacy, and insurance company schedules.

Qualifications
  • Degree, certification, or formal training in nursing, medical assisting, or another healthcare field.
  • Experience supporting psychiatric, behavioral health, telehealth, primary care, or specialty medical providers.
  • Familiarity with psychiatric medication terminology and medication-management processes.
  • Experience supporting physicians, nurse practitioners, or other prescribing providers.
  • Experience reviewing clinical documentation for prior authorization submissions.
  • Experience handling insurance denials, appeals, and follow-up.
  • Knowledge of gender-affirming care and LGBTQIA+ healthcare needs.
  • Experience with insurance verification, referrals, claims communication, or healthcare compliance.
  • Experience using Tebra, IntakeQ, Spruce, CoverMyMeds, or comparable platforms.
  • Medical office management experience.
  • Experience creating SOPs or improving administrative workflows.
  • Project coordination or healthcare operations management experience.

Benefits

  • Full-time role

  • 100% remote position

  • Opportunity to work in an inclusive, mission-driven mental health setting

  • Exposure to modern digital health platforms and patient communication tools

  • Collaborative, supportive work culture with space to grow professionally

jobs.title: Product Manager (Forward-Deployed)
jobs.excerpt: About Ume IntelligenceUme Intelligence is a marketing science company solving complex commercial problems for multi-location restaurant brands.
jobs.description:
About Ume Intelligence

Ume Intelligence is a marketing science company solving complex commercial problems for multi-location restaurant brands. We build modern analytics and automation infrastructure, paired with hands-on digital operations that turn operational data into measurable revenue.

We operate as a lean, high-leverage team with no walls between engineering and operations. We look for people who run toward technology, automation, and data models rather than away from them—and who evaluate success by real business impact (margin, demand, and net revenue) rather than vanity metrics or features shipped.

The Role

We are looking for a Forward-Deployed Product Manager to sit at the center of how Ume works: bridging our clients, our forward-deployed marketers, our founders, and our engineering team.

A restaurant brand’s demand comes from search, delivery marketplaces, its own customer database, and foot traffic past the door. These levers interact dynamically, yet restaurant operators lack the time to model any of it. You will own the software workflows that model these interactions and the operational mechanics that run on them every day.

When an operational edge case occurs for a client, you resolve it immediately and engineer safeguards so it cannot happen again. When an operator executes the same workflow manually for the third time, you convert it into a structured process, an automated check, or a software spec, and partner with engineering to build it.

This role starts with high-context individual ownership across product definition and client operations. As our deployment expands, the position is designed to transition into leading and scaling the team.

What You’ll Own

  • Client operations, end to end. Take complete ownership of client operational data (menus, pricing architectures, localized promotions, search listings, and CRM segments across delivery aggregators). Maintain zero tolerance for client-facing discrepancies.

  • Fix it, then prevent it. Catch issues before clients do. Trace each one to its cause and close the loop with a process change, an automated check, or a product fix, so the same problem does not come back.

  • Product Discovery and Specifications: Synthesize feedback directly from brand operators, growth marketers, and company founders into structured product specifications. Validate and accept engineering releases, measuring whether features moved targeted operational or commercial metrics.

  • Commercial and Unit Economics: Rigorously model client-level channel economics (net margins after commissions, ad discounts, and delivery fees) alongside internal unit economics (internal cost-to-serve per client account).

  • The Technical-Commercial Bridge: Partner daily with software engineers, forward-deployed marketers, and company leadership, spending dedicated hours each week directly with brand executives. Translate ambiguous business problems into crisp technical requirements and explain technical capabilities in terms of commercial lift.

  • Concurrent Program Delivery: Drive multiple client implementations, product features, and operational priorities in parallel without dropping critical details. Maintain clarity on which priority moves the needle each day.

  • Team and System Scalability: Design the operating cadences, playbooks, and onboarding standards as the company grows, helping evaluate, hire, and train future team members.

Your First 90 Days

  1. Day 30. You own day-to-day operations for at least one enterprise client account and have documented an end-to-end demand and margin map identifying key points of failure.

  2. Day 60. You have specified and shipped at least one software improvement with clear commercial or operational metrics attached.

  3. Day 90. You have eliminated a recurring class of client operational issues through an automated check or productized feature.

What You Bring

Experience & Background

  • Around 4+ years in product management, product operations, forward-deployed engineering/ops, or a high-rigor analytics/consulting role where you owned measurable outcomes rather than slide recommendations. Tenure is a benchmark, not a rigid constraint; demonstrated execution takes precedence.

  • Demonstrated experience working directly alongside engineering teams in a software company, venture-backed startup, digital agency or technical consulting environment.

  • Relevant academic grounding (Engineering, Economics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or Business). An MBA or advanced degree from a premier global program (e.g., IIMs, ISB, INSEAD, or reputed US/European/Asian business schools) is a strong advantage, though demonstrated judgment and execution track record remain the primary evaluation criteria.

Core Competencies & Must-Haves

  • Detail-Oriented: You spot the misconfigured price tier, the missing inventory item, and the conflicting campaign dates. You audit your own work before external stakeholders see it.

  • Business-Savvy: You understand multi-unit retail economics and know how marketing, localized pricing, and aggregator commissions interact with store P&Ls.

  • Technical Acumen: You are comfortable working with structured data schemas, spreadsheets, SQL-level data logic, platform APIs, and modern developer toolchains. You can debate technical trade-offs with engineers without needing to write production code.

  • Systems Thinking: You naturally look for recurring patterns and architectural solutions rather than settling for repetitive manual interventions.

  • Multi-Threading: You manage multiple concurrent operational threads cleanly, maintaining strict organization, proactive documentation, and clear stakeholder communication.

  • Leadership & Trust: You build rapid credibility with engineering leads, commercial marketers, and enterprise clients, demonstrating the ability to drive alignment without formal authority.

  • Executive Communication: Crisp, articulate written and spoken English. Much of our work is delivered through specifications, memos, and client updates, with frequent presentations directly to executive brand leadership.

Nice to Have

  • Domain background in restaurants, food & beverage networks, or multi-location retail brands.

  • Hands-on familiarity with third-party delivery marketplaces (DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub), local search/SEO ecosystems, or retention CRM architectures.

  • Experience with restaurant POS ecosystems, dynamic pricing engines, or revenue management systems.

  • Daily utilization of modern AI workflows (prompt frameworks, local automation scripts, LLM interfaces) to accelerate operational velocity.

  • Experience hiring, onboarding, or mentoring technical operators or junior product managers.

Working Hours

  • Full-time schedule with flexibility outside core touchpoints.

  • We expect dedicated collaboration hours with US clients and our forward-deployed marketers, typically between 6:00 AM and 12:00 PM US Pacific Time.

How Performance Is Measured

You will operate with modern automation tools, analytics infrastructure, and engineering resources. With that leverage comes a clear standard for analytical rigor, client impact, and operational discipline:

  • Execution Precision & Quality Assurance (35% Weight):
    In multi-location brand operations, accuracy across pricing, menu configurations, and campaign setups directly protects client margin and trust.
    Target: Zero high-severity client-facing defects on live accounts; 100% adherence to pre-launch validation workflows.

  • Product Impact & Workflow Leverage (30% Weight):
    Converting real operational friction into software specifications that remove bottlenecks and expand team throughput.
    Target: Identified problems successfully specified, accepted by engineering, and deployed; measurable reduction in manual operational time across client accounts.

  • Commercial Economics & Account Health (20% Weight):
    Measurable commercial improvements across client channels and internal cost-to-serve metrics.
    Target: Progress against client-specific net margin targets and proactive containment of account service costs.

  • Stakeholder Leadership & Dependability (15% Weight):
    Cross-functional trust with software engineers, marketing operators, and client leadership during core US collaboration windows.
    Target: Consistent schedule reliability during US Pacific overlap hours, proactive stakeholder communication, and high ratings across client and internal reviews.

What We Offer

  • Competitive Full-Time Compensation: Stable, competitive monthly base salary benchmarked for high-performing talent.

  • Meaningful Equity Participation: Opportunity to earn stock options and hold real equity upside in a venture-backed, high-growth US company as we scale.

  • Paid Time Off & Holidays: Generous paid annual leave plus observed corporate holidays.

  • A Path to Lead: Direct path to expand the forward-deployed product function and step into team leadership as organizational headcount grows.

  • High Leverage, Low Bureaucracy: Direct exposure to founders, clients, and core architecture in an environment with minimal meetings and zero political bloat.

At Talkspace, we are committed to fostering a diverse, equitable, inclusive, and belonging-centered workplace where everyone can thrive while making a difference in mental health. Want to help over two million people receive quality mental healthcare? Come join our mission to get therapy into the hands of everyone!

We’re looking for a part-time, contract Therapist (Independent Contract Provider) who is passionate about reaching individuals who need mental healthcare but lack easy access to it. This role is perfect for those seeking the opportunity to work with a diverse client base while enjoying the flexibility and rewards of private practice—without the hassle of administrative work. Let Talkspace handle the insurance billing, marketing, and administrative costs, so you can create your own schedule and focus fully on providing impactful care!

What you'll do:

About you

    • Licensed Professional Clinical Counselor - Supervisor (LPCC-S)
  • Individual professional malpractice liability insurance policy
  • Individual NPI number
  • Comfortable learning new online tools and technology
  • Reliable internet connection and video-capable device

Perks

  • Clients Ready for You: Talkspace provides new client referrals
  • Flexible Schedule: Set your own schedule with no minimum requirement for your weekly hours or caseload size
  • No Membership Fees: No provider fees
  • Accept Insurance Without Hassle: Talkspace will take care of all aspects of client insurance including credentialing, billing, and claims
  • Everything in One Place: Sessions, clinical documentation, resources, and compensation tracking on one platform
  • Fully Paid Training: Master the Talkspace platform before your first session
  • Clinical Support: Provider Support and IT teams available for any technical or platform related questions
  • Free CEUs: NBCC and ASWB accredited continuing education credits via Talkspace-provided Learning Communities
  • Health Perks: Access Stride Health to support your health and financial well-being

Compensation

  • $70 per hour for live chat, audio, or video sessions (this rate is prorated for 45 and 30 minute sessions)
  • Additional compensation for asynchronous messaging
  • Earn a new client engagement bonus, varying by plan type

Please note: If you treat clients in multiple states, different rates will apply accordingly. Rates could be subject to change and may vary over time based on the market and shifts in demand.

Why Talkspace

Talkspace is a leading virtual behavioral healthcare provider committed to helping people lead healthier, happier lives through access to high-quality mental healthcare. At Talkspace, we believe that mental healthcare is core to overall health and should be available to everyone.

Talkspace pioneered the ability to text with a licensed therapist from anywhere and now offers a comprehensive suite of mental health services, including therapy for individuals, teens, and couples, as well as psychiatric treatment and medication management (18+). With Talkspace’s core therapy offerings, members are matched with one of thousands of licensed therapists within days and can engage in live video, audio, or chat sessions, and/or unlimited asynchronous text messaging sessions.

All care offered at Talkspace is delivered through an easy-to-use, fully-encrypted web and mobile platform that meets HIPAA, federal, and state regulatory requirements. More than 151 million Americans have access to Talkspace through their health insurance plans, employee assistance programs, our partnerships with leading healthcare companies, or as a free benefit through their employer, school, or government agency.

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

Talkspace welcomes and celebrates talent from all backgrounds, perspectives, and walks of life to foster an innovative and diverse workforce. We encourage you to apply, even if you don’t meet every qualification or if your path has been nontraditional — such as not completing a formal degree program, taking a career break, or having a prior criminal record — if you believe you could make a great addition to this team. Come as you are and learn about the exciting opportunities on our team.

Individuals seeking employment at Talkspace are considered without regard to race, color, religious creed, sex, national origin, citizenship status, age, physical or mental disability, sexual orientation, marital, parental, veteran or military status, unfavorable military discharge, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state or local law.

How do we define Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging at Talkspace?

Diversity

Diversity encompasses the unique attributes of our employees as individuals. We value and embrace the richness arising from their varied backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences, which include, but are not limited to, age, ability, ethnicity, gender, race, and cultural background.

Equity

Equity refers to a fair and impartial workplace, aiming to ensure equal growth and advancement opportunities for all employees. This involves amplifying underrepresented voices, addressing unconscious biases, and providing inclusive, culturally competent mental health care.

Inclusion

Inclusion signifies the practice of granting equal access to opportunities and resources for all employees, particularly those who might otherwise be excluded or marginalized. It ensures that everyone feels a sense of belonging, value, support, and respect as an individual.

Belonging

Belonging reflects the affinity and positive relationships that develop among employees from diverse backgrounds when businesses actively promote diversity, equity, and inclusion in the workplace.

About No deviation

At No deviation, we are dedicated to delivering patient-centric solutions that revolutionize the pharmaceutical landscape. As a dynamic expert in engineering consultancy, Commissioning Qualification Validation (CQV), and Quality, Compliance, and Regulatory services, we are looking for individuals who are excited to contribute to impactful projects and drive innovation.

Position Overview

We are seeking an experienced IT/OT Project Lead to lead the assessment, planning, and implementation readiness for a site-wide upgrade of OT computerized systems to Windows 11 LTSC. The environment includes approximately 70+ GMP and non-GMP OT system assets distributed across Manufacturing, QC Laboratories, and Development Laboratories. The role will initially focus on conducting a comprehensive current-state assessment and developing a detailed, phased project roadmap covering technical feasibility, system dependencies, resource requirements, cost estimates, timelines, risks, procurement requirements, and implementation strategy. The successful candidate should have sufficient technical understanding of OT infrastructure, computerized systems, and regulated manufacturing environments to effectively engage with Engineering, Manufacturing, QC, IT/OT, Quality, vendors, and system integrators.

  • Assess system readiness and compatibility for migration to Windows 11 LTSC.
  • Identify technical gaps, obsolescence risks, cybersecurity concerns, dependencies, and upgrade constraints.
  • Engage equipment vendors, application vendors, and system integrators to confirm Windows 11 compatibility, hardware requirements, software/application upgrade requirements, licensing requirements, and vendor support requirements.
  • Define a risk-based and phased upgrade strategy for the site.

  • Develop business case and budgetary estimates for project approval.
  • Define implementation sequencing to minimise impact to manufacturing and laboratory operations.
  • Develop the proposed approach for testing, commissioning, system verification/qualification, cutover, rollback, and operational handover.
  • Coordinate stakeholders across Engineering, Manufacturing Operations, QC, Development Labs, IT/OT, Quality, and vendors.
  • Establish project governance, risk tracking, and management reporting.
  • Support vendor selection, technical evaluation, and tender/RFP activities where required.

  • Ability to work across both technical and business stakeholders.
  • Strong project planning, cost estimation, risk management, and stakeholder management capabilities.
  • Experience coordinating equipment vendors, software vendors, and system integrators.
  • Familiarity with project planning tools such as Microsoft Project, Primavera, or equivalent.

Why join us?

jobs.title: Head of Paid Social, Insurance
jobs.excerpt: WHO ARE WE? Launch Potato is the discovery and conversion company.
jobs.description:
WHO ARE WE?

Launch Potato is the discovery and conversion company. We reach tens of millions of people every month through our brands, including FinanceBuzz, All About Cookies, and OnlyInYourState. We turn that attention into real outcomes for our partners, some of the world's leading companies.

Our mission: create predictable, high-value customer acquisition at scale by connecting discovery, intent, and performance across category-leading consumer brands in finance, travel, and entertainment.

We run profitable and bootstrapped, with a South Florida HQ and a remote-first team across 18 countries.

WHY JOIN US?

You own outcomes here, not tasks. We measure work by impact, not activity. The pace is real, and change is constant, so the people who do best turn change into opportunity instead of waiting for it to settle. Feedback runs direct and lands with respect. Ordinary people make themselves extraordinary at Launch Potato.

Auto insurance on paid social is one of our highest-potential channels and you would own it end to end taking it to the next level.

This is a hands-on seat. You are in Ads Manager daily, pulling your own numbers, setting the testing agenda with the creative team, and staying with a test through launch, read, and post-mortem. If you are looking to hand a strategy deck to someone else to execute, this is not it.

The honest trade: the channel has proven scale and a real ceiling. Creative fatigues fast, attribution is noisy, and regulation reshapes what you can say and where you can send traffic. Those problems are yours. Nobody is going to solve them above you.

Why This Seat

You own a vertical, not a slice. Meta and TikTok spend for auto insurance, end to end, from budget and bid strategy to the creative roadmap to live margin performance. One owner, and it is you.

Margin is the metric. Not impressions, not a ROAS number handed down without context. You decide when to push into a lower ROAS for contribution dollars and when to pull back, and you are trusted to make that call.

The mandate is scale, not maintenance. The plan is to grow this channel to roughly 2.5x its current monthly spend without giving up margin. That is the job. If you want a channel that is already solved, this is the wrong one.

The interesting part is unsolved. Creative fatigue cycles, attribution noise, and compliance constraints on a vertical with real headroom. You will not be maintaining someone else's playbook. You will be writing the one the rest of the team runs.

Short line to the people who decide. You work directly with the Senior Director who owns paid marketing, the GM of Auto Insurance, compliance, and product. No layers to route a recommendation through.

Profitable and bootstrapped. Spend decisions here get made on margin, not against a burn plan set by someone else's timeline.

What You'll Bring

  • Paid social bought at scale in performance marketing, affiliate, or leadgen. Not brand work and not agency-of-record media planning.
  • Deep hands-on Meta expertise: campaign structure, bid and budget strategy, audience and placement testing, and diagnosing a performance shift caused by a platform or attribution change rather than by your campaigns.
  • Real TikTok scale, not test budgets. You have managed meaningful spend through allowlisting, vertical restrictions, and landing page requirements.
  • Direct accountability for CPA, ROAS, or contribution margin on monthly spend of $250,000 or more.
  • Experience in a compliance-heavy vertical such as insurance, lending, credit, or health, where creative and landing page claims are constrained.
  • Fluency with tracking and attribution: pixel and server-side event setup, postbacks, conversion QA, and the judgment to spot when the data is lying to you.
  • Four or more years in a hands-on, in-the-weeds buying role with direct margin accountability.

How we work, and what we look for in how you work:

  • Focus and Win. You start from the P&L and the metric, not the tactic, and you are relentless about why performance moved. You do not stop at the first explanation.
  • Better Every Day. You seek feedback and turn it into visible change, and you write down what you learn so the next buyer does not relearn it.
  • Stronger Together. You brief the creative team clearly, give specific feedback, and treat them as partners in the testing agenda rather than a request queue. You surface a problem early with a recommendation attached instead of waiting to be asked.
  • Embrace Change. When a platform policy or a compliance constraint moves, you find the compliant path to scale rather than stopping at no.

Nice to Have

  • Auto insurance, or another regulated leadgen domain
  • Advertorial or direct-response landing page funnels and conversion rate testing
  • Working knowledge of AI creative generation tooling
  • Familiarity with Looker

What You'll Own

  • Meta and TikTok spend for auto insurance, end to end, with measurable margin impact. You have a teammate on the buying team who can support execution when volume calls for it, and the ownership stays with you.
  • Pacing and margin targets, including the judgment call on when lower ROAS is the right trade for contribution dollars.
  • The creative testing roadmap, built with the Creative Strategist and the creative team and turned into shipped concepts at high velocity.
  • A documented, repeatable playbook other buyers on the team can run.
  • Direct relationships with Meta and TikTok reps, and the allowlisting, beta access, and escalation paths a restricted vertical depends on.
  • The working partnership with the GM of Auto Insurance, compliance, and product on funnel, landing page, and offer strategy.

What Great Looks Like

By the end of your first year:

  • Auto insurance paid social hits its margin and pacing targets consistently, and you can explain every miss without being asked.
  • Monthly spend is materially higher than when you started, and margin held.
  • Creative test velocity is up and the win rate is better, because the roadmap is deliberate instead of reactive.
  • Your testing playbook is in use by other buyers on the team.
  • Meta and TikTok reps take your call, and you have unlocked at least one thing for this vertical that the team did not have access to before.
  • Compliance and product treat you as a partner on funnel and offer strategy rather than as a request coming in.

This Isn't the Right Seat If You

  • Want to set strategy and hand execution to someone else. This role is in the account daily.
  • Have only bought inside an agency with no accountability for margin or profit.
  • Need a stable platform environment. Policy, creative fatigue, and attribution all shift here, sometimes in the same week.
  • Treat compliance as the reason something cannot be done rather than a constraint to solve within.
  • Prefer to work a problem quietly and present a finished answer. We would rather hear it early and rough.

Want to accelerate your career? Apply now!

We do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics.

jobs.excerpt: Why Charlie Health? Millions of people across the country are navigating mental health conditions, substance use disorders, and eating disorders, but too often, they’re met with barriers to care.
jobs.description:
Why Charlie Health?

Millions of people across the country are navigating mental health conditions, substance use disorders, and eating disorders, but too often, they’re met with barriers to care. From limited local options and long wait times to treatment that lacks personalization, behavioral healthcare can leave people feeling unseen and unsupported.

Charlie Health exists to change that. Our mission is to connect the world to life-saving behavioral health treatment. We deliver personalized, virtual care rooted in connection—between clients and clinicians, care teams, loved ones, and the communities that support them. By focusing on people with complex needs, we’re expanding access to meaningful care and driving better outcomes from the comfort of home.

As a rapidly growing organization, we're reaching more communities every day and building a team that’s redefining what behavioral health treatment can look like. If you're ready to use your skills to drive lasting change and help more people access the care they deserve, we’d love to meet you.

About the Role

Core Platform is a platform team. Our customers are Charlie Health's other engineering teams, and our job is to make them faster, safer, and more consistent. We don't ship product features. We build the patterns, services, and guardrails that other engineering teams depend on.

As a Staff Platform Engineer on Core Platform, you will own our Core Services for our system and one of the pillars of our AI-Native SDLC initiative: quality gates and test foundations, safe automated delivery, or AI-assisted development. You will take your area from design through production operation, and the patterns you set become the team's paved roads.

Every engineer is a tech lead, and as a Staff engineer you are a domain owner: people come to you with the hardest technical decisions in your area, and you make calls that hold up across team boundaries. You will work alongside a team of experienced engineers who own the platform primitives. We build with AI as the default. Plans are the primary input, agents draft most of the implementation, and the quality gates this team owns make it safe in a HIPAA-regulated clinical business.

Responsibilities

  • Own one or more platform or SDLC primitives end to end, from architecture and build through production operation and long-term evolution
  • Build the deterministic quality gates that let agent-written code ship safely: automated end-to-end testing, golden test datasets, and schema change safety
  • Roll out AI code review safely, and contribute to the organization’s best-practices guide for AI-assisted development
  • Deliver core services on the team's own paved roads, finding the potholes before any product squad does
  • Mature authentication and authorization standards across the platform, including agent identity: scoped, short-lived, audited credentials for non-human principals
  • Write plans that name invariants, error cases, security implications, and acceptance criteria, and orchestrate agents across hard multi-PR work
  • Coach Senior engineers and product squad engineers on agentic engineering best practices and platform patterns
  • Define the reliability conventions for your area: SLO definitions, observability standards, and incident response practice, including a seat in the on-call rotation
  • Steward the security and compliance posture of your primitive, and stay aware of what it costs to run
  • Document the standards in your domain as architecture decision records and bring them through our Architecture Advice Guild

Requirements

  • 7+ years of software engineering experience, including several years designing and operating distributed systems or platform components that other teams build on
  • Depth in at least one of these areas: test automation at scale (unit and integration standards, end-to-end coverage of critical flows, flake control), enabling AI code review at scale, or authorization systems with ReBAC and RBAC models (Auth0 FGA, Zanzibar, OpenFGA, Cedar, or similar)
  • Experience with skills, MCPs, harnesses, agentic tooling ecosystems, or agent orchestration for software development
  • You build with AI agents as part of your daily work. You write plans that agents can implement, run agents for real delivery, and know where agent output needs human judgment
  • Experience with data modeling for systems of record, including safe schema changes against live production data
  • Proficiency in the stack we run: Python and/or TypeScript services, Postgres, and AWS
  • A track record of driving workstreams that span multiple engineers and quarters without people authority
  • Comfort operating production critical-path systems, including on-call, in a regulated environment
  • Clear, direct communication with engineers, product partners, and leadership
  • This is a remote role. Our teams work across time zones and are available during core meeting hours (12PM to 5PM EST)

Nice to Haves

  • Progressive delivery tooling (feature flags, canary deployments) and end-to-end frameworks such as Playwright at scale
  • Healthcare data standards (FHIR, HL7v2) and engineering in a HIPAA-regulated environment
  • An incremental monolith-to-services migration you led
  • Time on a platform or developer experience team
  • Fluency with domain-driven design or event storming

Benefits

Charlie Health is pleased to offer comprehensive benefits to all full-time, exempt employees. Read more about our benefits here.

The total target base compensation for this role will be between $185,000 and $265,000 per year at the commencement of employment. Please note, pay will be determined on an individualized basis and will be impacted by location, experience, expertise, internal pay equity, and other relevant business considerations. Further, cash compensation is only part of the total compensation package, which, depending on the position, may include stock options and other Charlie Health-sponsored benefits.

Our Values

  • Connection: Care deeply & inspire hope.
  • Congruence: Stay curious & heed the evidence.
  • Commitment: Act with urgency & don’t give up.

Please do not call our public clinical admissions line in regard to this or any other job posting.

Please be cautious of potential recruitment fraud. If you are interested in exploring opportunities at Charlie Health, please go directly to our Careers Page: Charlie Health will never ask you to pay a fee or download software as part of the interview process with our company. In addition, Charlie Health will not ask for your personal banking information until you have signed an offer of employment and completed onboarding paperwork that is provided by our People Operations team. All communications with Charlie Health Talent and People Operations professionals will only be sent from @charliehealth.com email addresses. Legitimate emails will never originate from gmail.com, yahoo.com, or other commercial email services.

Recruiting agencies, please do not submit unsolicited referrals for this or any open role. We have a roster of agencies with whom we partner, and we will not pay any fee associated with unsolicited referrals.

At Charlie Health, we value being an Equal Opportunity Employer. We strive to cultivate an environment where individuals can be their authentic selves. Being an Equal Opportunity Employer means every member of our team feels as though they are supported and belong. We value diverse perspectives to help us provide essential mental health and substance use disorder treatments to all young people.

Charlie Health applicants are assessed solely on their qualifications for the role, without regard to disability or need for accommodation.

Location & work modality: Remote

About Radian Arc.

Radian Arc delivers AI infrastructure and GPU-as-a-Service (GPUaaS) solutions that enable enterprises, telecommunications operators, governments, and AI organizations to deploy, operate, and scale high-performance GPU infrastructure. With teams across the USA, Australia, Europe, Malaysia, Singapore, and Japan, we work with customers and strategic partners to deliver platforms for enterprise AI, sovereign AI, inference, training, and next-generation GPU cloud services.

What impact you will have

We are looking for a Senior Project Manager to own complex, multi-stakeholder GPUaaS and AI infrastructure deployments from planning through production handover. You will set the plan, critical path, and delivery governance for each deployment. You will coordinate Solutions Architecture, Engineering, Product, Procurement, Data Center Operations, Service Delivery, Sales, customers, vendors, and strategic partners, and keep delivery aligned with customer expectations and commercial commitments.

You will also play a key role in building Radian Arc's Project Management Office (PMO). That means designing and standardizing how we deploy, and applying automation and AI-assisted development tools to turn those processes into repeatable workflows and live dashboards, with less manual coordination as deployment volume grows.

This is a highly autonomous role for someone who enjoys creating structure in a fast-growing company. You will work with teams across the USA, Europe, Asia, and Australia, so you will regularly need to collaborate outside standard business hours.

What you’ll do:

Deployment Delivery

  • Own end-to-end delivery of GPUaaS, AI infrastructure, hardware, and new data center / PoP deployments, from initial planning through production handover.
  • Build and maintain the integrated deployment plan and critical path across all workstreams: scope, timelines, milestones, dependencies, owners, risks, decisions, and completion criteria.
  • Coordinate hardware procurement, site readiness, installation, networking, storage, compute, platform deployment, and customer onboarding across internal teams and external partners.
  • Keep solution and engineering requirements, hardware delivery, site and operational readiness, customer commitments, and target production dates aligned.
  • Lead deployment acceptance, go-live readiness, stabilization, and formal handover into Service Delivery and Operations.
  • Manage multiple deployments in parallel, balancing shared resources, dependencies, and competing priorities.

Deployment Process Design and Governance

  • Define Radian Arc's standard deployment lifecycle, including stages, owners, required inputs, approval gates, and entry/exit criteria for each phase.
  • Establish delivery governance, including project kickoffs, readiness reviews, change control, decision logs, and escalation paths.
  • Create practical templates, checklists, and runbooks so new deployments start quickly and run consistently.
  • Help build Radian Arc's PMO by setting project-management standards and delivery disciplines that scale across customers, regions, and data center environments.
  • Run post-deployment reviews and feed lessons learned back into the standard process.

Automation, Dashboards, and Reporting

  • Use AI-assisted development and automation tools, such as Claude Code, to build, document, and continuously improve deployment workflows and project-management processes.
  • Work with Engineering to connect deployment workflows to Radian Arc systems, tools, and data sources, and automate routine coordination, tracking, reporting, and data updates wherever practical.
  • Build a standardized, shareable dashboard for each deployment, generated directly from workflow data so status is never maintained twice.
  • Provide executive and working-level views of scope, procurement status, milestones, dependencies, blockers, decisions, owners, and next actions, as a single source of truth throughout the project lifecycle.

Risk, Issues, and Stakeholder Communication

  • Identify risks, blockers, resource constraints, and dependency conflicts early, and drive mitigation, escalation, and cross-team resolution.
  • Provide clear, consistent status reporting to internal leadership, customers, vendors, and partners, and run regular project reviews, readiness reviews, and executive updates.
  • Translate complex technical, operational, procurement, and delivery issues into concise updates, clear decisions, and actionable next steps.
  • Build trusted relationships with customer, partner, and vendor stakeholders at both working and executive levels.

What success looks like:

In your first 90 days, you will:

  • Own active deployments, with an integrated plan, critical path, and risk register in place for each.
  • Document version 1 of Radian Arc's standard deployment lifecycle, including stages, owners, gates, and completion criteria.
  • Stand up a live dashboard for each active deployment that updates from workflow data rather than by hand.

Within six months, you will:

  • Have the standard deployment process in use across all new deployments.
  • Have measurably reduced the manual effort spent on coordination, tracking, and status reporting

What you'll need

  • 7+ years in project management, program management, technical delivery, or infrastructure deployment roles, including 5+ years managing complex infrastructure deployments involving multiple internal teams, vendors, partners, and customers.
  • 3+ years working with AI infrastructure, GPU platforms, cloud infrastructure, data centers, hardware deployments, telecommunications operators, or managed infrastructure services.
  • A track record of owning deployments end to end, with direct responsibility for timelines, dependencies, and delivery outcomes, from hardware procurement and site readiness through go-live and handover to operations.
  • Experience building or improving PMO processes, project governance, reporting frameworks, dashboards, and standardized delivery processes.
  • Demonstrated ability to design and improve integrated project workflows, with a practical understanding of how automation, APIs, workflow tools, and AI-assisted development tools can reduce manual coordination and reporting.
  • Technical fluency across compute, networking, storage, data center, platform, and operational workstreams: enough to challenge a plan, spot a missing dependency, and earn engineers' trust.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, including with customers and executives.
  • Experience working with distributed teams across multiple countries and time zones.

Nice to have:

  • Hands-on experience building workflow automation, integrations, or AI-assisted tooling using scripting, APIs, workflow platforms, Claude Code, or similar tools.
  • Direct experience deploying GPU clusters or other high-performance compute environments.
  • Experience with telecommunications operators, or with government or sovereign AI programs.
  • Experience at a fast-growing company where you built delivery processes from scratch.
  • PMP, PRINCE2, or Agile/Scrum certification

What we offer

• Attractive compensation package reflecting your expertise and experience.
• A great work environment characterised by friendliness, international diversity, flexibility, and a hybrid-friendly approach.
• You'll be part of a fast-growing scale-up with a mission to make a positive impact, offering an exciting career evolution.

Our job titles may span more than one job level. The actual base pay is dependent on a number of factors, such as transferable skills, work experience, business needs and market demands.

Our inclusive responsibility

jobs.excerpt: We're looking for a Senior Data Analyst who's equally happy designing an experiment, arguing about what a metric actually means or modelling data.
jobs.description:
We're looking for a Senior Data Analyst who's equally happy designing an experiment, arguing about what a metric actually means or modelling data. You'll own the analysis behind how we decide things — which tests are worth running in collaboration with our stakeholders, what the results actually say, and what we should do next — or help build AI Analyst, our internal MCP that lets anyone ask the data a question without filing a ticket. Your work will shape the numbers the company steers by, from the product North Star to the leading indicators that tell us where revenue is heading before it gets there. You'll work across product, marketing, R&D and revenue, alongside a small, senior data team and our engineers, using SQL, dbt, Looker and Python. If you like broad problems, short paths to impact, and having your recommendation actually change what happens — you'll feel right at home.

🚀 What you'll do

  • Drive high-impact projects end to end — from a vague business question to a shipped outcome. We'll agree the why and the what together; the how is yours.
  • Design and assess experiments — judge whether an A/B test is viable in the first place, design it properly when it is, and build a credible pre/post or quasi-experimental read when it isn't
  • Analyse experiments honestly and say what they mean — including the ones that didn't work, and the ones where the data can't carry the conclusion someone wants
  • Make recommendations, not just dashboards — a big part of this role is landing a point of view: what we should do, why, and what you'd need to see to change your mind
  • Define the metrics the company steers by — and how are they impacted by the different levers we have to achieve our goals
  • Build the datasets and models the rest of us rely on — ETL/ELT transformations, curated datasets per business use case, and our migration to dbt
  • Help build AI Analyst, our internal MCP, so stakeholders can self-serve answers — and partner closely with product, marketing, R&D and engineering, keeping expectations managed and flagging delays early with a reason and a new date

👏 We're looking for someone who has

  • Solid senior-level experience as a data analyst in SaaS — you know NDR, expansion, contraction and MRR as things you've modelled, not terms you've heard
  • Real experimentation depth — you've designed, sized and analysed A/B tests, you know when a clean test isn't possible and what you'd do instead, and you're comfortable being the person who says a result isn't significant
  • A habit of ending with a recommendation — you're analytical and opinionated, you tell people what you think they should do based on evidence, and you're clear about how confident you are
  • Expert SQL, Python for the work SQL can't do, and comfort in Looker (or a close equivalent) for getting insight in front of people
  • Strong data modelling and analytics engineering — you build the layer everyone else relies on rather than just querying it, with real dbt mileage
  • A genuine appetite for AI — you're already using it in your workflow and curious about what it changes for analytics
  • Generalist range and real autonomy — you move between product, marketing, R&D and revenue questions, drive your own projects, know who to ask when you're stuck, and don't stall when priorities shift in a lean remote team

➕ Bonus points, if you have

  • Data science experience — building ML models and getting them into production
  • Experience at principal or staff level; we're open to those levels for the right person

📍 Where you'll work

Remote, from anywhere within CET ±1 — including the EU, UK, Ukraine and South Africa. Hours are flexible, with a general expectation that you're available and responsive across CET 9–5. Flexibility works both ways.

🎁 What we offer

  • 22 days of paid time off, plus your local national holidays
  • Flexible work hours and a culture that trusts you to manage your time
  • Private medical insurance or a medical allowance (depending on your location)
  • Extended paid sick leave so you can fully recover without worry
  • Career map with growth opportunities
  • A quarterly learning budget for courses, books, or anything that helps you grow professionally
  • A quarterly wellbeing budget you can use for sport, therapy, or even a good novel
  • Best hardware for your work (team Apple)
  • An award-winning product loved by thousands of customers worldwide
  • A transparent, flexible culture with people at the core of everything we do
  • Events that are actually fun
